editorial_policy: ONE manuscript island and port led; previous integrated v0.1, standalone global GEB and standalone island-port JBI texts are source archives and are not to be submitted independently in parallel
journal_target: Global Ecology and Biogeography first, Journal of Biogeography as a later alternative for the SAME article only
source_separation: 225 original candidate butterflies×51 WPI-associated GSHHG landmass source; 199 trait-complete, 111 indirect migration list positives
98 botanical-effort-covered insular regions and 51-landmass pairs do not share population
No private 83573-row original Parquet was accessed
1596 completed ports from 3630 source catalogued across 142 country codes with 687 introduced candidate host taxa; do not infer 1596 island-only ports
Historical original230 2001–2010 plant × 2011–2017 butterfly source is a distinct 113-event cohort and not directly the 208/1163 pooled-pair cohort
51-landmass butterfly-host pair ρ .300 and 225-species rho .652 share HOSTS/WCVP-derived source identity but retain different species and geographic grains
Original port 17 × 5km local butterfly co-index is not a matched port versus nonport host comparison
Original 51-island 1275-pair host×marine conditional held-island prediction is NOT original 225×51 first-index species-island model; predictor inputs span different dates.
Double-endpoint geographically unseen marine prediction uses 990 early-general-plant-indexed pairs; cannot exchange MSE gains or claims with 51 leave-one-island-out 1275-pair study.
17-island 24 paired port/nonport coastal study comes from distinct PR #158, selects ports using >=30 pre2011 plant records, and uses new remote 5km controls, NOT original 2021 landcover controls.

claims.population: 126 strict insular and 237 mainland WGSRPD3 regions
claims.interpretation: Potential butterfly×region cell gains; not direct population benefits

claims.population: 15 comparable WGSRPD3 Level1×area strata
claims.interpretation: Supported overlap strata; not experimental difference

claims.population: 3630 original WPI port candidates; 1596 with complete botanical GBIF queries across 142 country codes
claims.interpretation: Surveyed port-buffer plant index and regional modern WCVP origin; no offport contrast, recorded introduction year or ship cargo

claims.population: 98 botanical-effort-covered insular WCVP regions
claims.interpretation: Three separate association models; not selective sea transport or mediation

claims.population: 10 leading global butterfly resource-contribution plants; 17 sampled landmass groups with 38 WPI port buffers 2001–2010
claims.interpretation: Earlier recorded accepted plant taxa, not historical island-specific introduced status, larval resource use, observed carriage or fraction of global resource gain realized

claims.population: 239 butterflies × WGSRPD3 resource units
claims.interpretation: Potential host-resource availability; not butterfly occupancy or abundance

claims.population: 239 butterflies, host-family diet breadth
claims.interpretation: Estimated small association; exact zero/equivalence not established

claims.population: 670 contributing butterfly larval-host plants
claims.interpretation: Fractional attribution of potential opportunity, not observed feeding

claims.population: 239 butterflies, FAO crop-host exclusions
claims.interpretation: Non-crop opportunity persists; not a species-level weed mechanism

claims.population: 225 butterfly host/port crosswalk species; 2001–2024 pooled plant candidate indices
claims.interpretation: Strong descriptive species-level bridge with overlapping HOSTS and WCVP taxonomies and possibly post-outcome port host records; NOT a transport effect

claims.population: 82 butterflies and 1163 shared first-index butterfly × pair combinations among 51 original port-linked landmass groups
claims.interpretation: Positive butterfly×port candidate host catalogue compatibility above host family/degree-only randomization; host-list geography, plant source era and true feeding NOT controlled

claims.population: 17 originally sampled 5-km port buffers; butterfly coordinates and host candidate records pooled 2001–2024
claims.interpretation: Real butterfly and candidate larval host records in same port buffer; no observed feeding, yearly correspondence, host identity overlap 51-pair test or matched off-port species controls

claims.population: 225 candidate butterflies, 51 landmass groups, 1275 non-independent island pairs
claims.interpretation: Retrospective community correspondence; earlier stronger so no causal botanical arrival order

claims.population: 155 recorded butterfly species, 208482 held-period combinations
claims.interpretation: Retrospective index recording prediction, not pre-introduction host chronology; species-unseen transfer not supported

claims.population: Strict geographical subset of original 155-species forecast: 95 species and 39753 score rows in 12 of 51 island groups
claims.interpretation: Positive host recording predictor in island-score subset but 97.2% rows Britain/Ireland; nested retrospective check, not independent 51-island replication

claims.population: 32 climate-stratified butterflies, 31 with indexed records
claims.interpretation: Presence-index overlap, not observed larval feeding/establishment

claims.population: 17 studied island groups, 113 butterfly first-index event cells from 60 butterflies in 2011–2017 and 2001–2010 original port botanical indexing
claims.interpretation: 34 authentic earlier compatible host plant index records in the same study island, but no extraordinary host matching after geographic/prevalence null; not same sample as 208/1163

claims.population: 113 butterfly 2011–2017 first-index cases with status of earlier compatible 2001–2010 island-port host indexing
claims.interpretation: No observed enhancement in subsequent indexing for earlier compatible host-record group; nonindex=unknown not absence; rerecord not reproduction or abundance

claims.population: 225 butterflies × original 51 landmass recording panel
claims.interpretation: New public GBIF source, no biological absence or true arrival; different from private 83573-row original

claims.population: 199 complete LepTraits butterflies, prior conspecific indexed sources among 51 sampled groups
claims.interpretation: Source conditional indices; nearest sampled prior source not true biological origin

claims.population: 199-trait-subset, constrained event location null, 2018–2022
claims.interpretation: Conditional null alignment, not independent prediction or causal movement

claims.population: 2018–2022 geographic cluster holdout, 51 landmass source
claims.interpretation: Modelled sea resistance worsens geographic transfer beyond distance

claims.population: 199 LepTraits butterflies, 2018–2022, three holdouts
claims.interpretation: Wing size proxy is not independently measured dispersal ability; no universal size×ocean effect

claims.population: 225 butterflies, 111 author-listed indirect migratory candidates, 114 migration unknown
claims.interpretation: 2021 review supplementary roster unavailable; author 2025 GBIF positive-list only; lacks non-migrant comparator

claims.population: 51-island holdout pairwise Jaccard
claims.interpretation: Different response and baseline from binary first-index; AIS/wind noncausal

claims.population: AIS local graph-label placebo and historical liner index
claims.interpretation: Shipping-specific mechanism cannot be isolated from local geography

claims.population: Cross-grain historical butterfly × larval host × island × year
claims.interpretation: No direct temporal preceding introduced larval-host presence, documented feeding, breeding, colonisation or shipborne stage

claims.population: 51 original GSHHG landmass groups, 1,275 dependent island pairs, 51 leave-one-island-out held island folds, later 2011-2022 butterfly Jaccard
claims.interpretation: Two conditional retrospective model improvements in the same 51 island-heldout folds, not independent causal effects, source-true future or ship transport. G->HC result recompute from original exact CSV.

claims.population: 990 early-botanically-indexed original island pairs, 15 both-island-endpoints-unseen geographic folds
claims.interpretation: Limited positive AIS-only late butterfly community increment conditional on retrospective hosts, but adverse joint AIS/wind and earlier community targets; AIS modern and not historical transport.

claims.population: 126 strict insular WGSRPD3 regions, potential butterfly×region resource opportunities
claims.interpretation: 54.3% of contemporary island potential known-host opportunity units are additions attributed to introduced plant ranges. Not an observed diet or abundance fraction.

claims.population: 17 distinct selected island groups, 24 matched port vs newly rebuilt non-port 5-km coastal zones, 2001-2010 plant indices and later butterfly indices
claims.interpretation: Source held in distinct Draft PR #158; negative exploratory port-selective correspondence with serious host-status, observation-effort, habitat and sampling bias. Different controls from ESA 2021.

claims.population: 225 butterfly x 51 source landmasses, 199 trait matched and 83 source qualified late 2018-2022 species-island indexes
claims.interpretation: Residual ocean observational association differs from heldout predictive generalization and from AIS/wind pairwise community model; no actual flight or colonisation.

prohibitions: Do not identify butterfly host opportunity with actual occurrence or reproduction
Do not report 111 author-selected migrant candidates versus 114 UNKNOWN species as migrant versus nonmigrant
Do not represent first GBIF index as true arrival or an earlier source as actual exporter
Do not infer shipborne host propagation, colonial trading paths or steppingstone hubs from uniform-ocean electrical circuits
Do not merge +54.9%, +118.9% and +40.9% as independent repeated biological gains
Do not claim wing-size modulation of sea resistance is robust or a measured flight ability
Do not count 1275 island pairs as 1275 independent islands
Do not present a unified causal chain, given no historically prior species-specific host×island×year exposure
Do not sum C->HC (+1.731%), H->HC (+6.488%) and G->HC (+8.616%), which use different baselines.
Do not represent retrospective held-island joint host/marine model as independent new geographic-region transfer or source-year prospectively usable predictors.
Do not call marine predictors independent causal determinants of butterfly accessibility or plant shipping; AIS is a modern spatial raster.
Do not treat positive AIS-only +0.678% in 990-pair double-unseen panel as robust joint AIS/wind effect; AIS+wind is negative.
central_question: How is human-redistributed known-host opportunity amplified on islands, what broad flora do ports index, and do recorded butterfly communities show complementary host and marine-geographic structure?
priority: 1 disproportionate 126-island potential resource amplification +118.9% (+10.7pp matched) within global 239 butterflies +54.9%
2 broad 1596-port introduced flora/98 botanical region associations; host-selective beta not positive
3 butterfly species names, candidate host island community similarity +0.300 and 155-species recording prediction +4.12%/+3.00%
4 original 51-island same-fold joint host/marine conditional positive MSE gains +1.731% and +6.488%
5 990-pair geographic transfer negative tests, 17-island port/nonport null and historic 34/113 host-exposure null prevent causal host-rescue claim
